_meta.description: Document-rules config for habeas_corpus — Petition for writ of habeas corpus under Article 226 (HC) / Article 32 (SC). The great writ of liberty — challenges illegal/unlawful custody. Most urgent writ; relaxed locus; usually listed within 24-48 hours.
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Sunil Batra, A.K. Roy, Rekha v. Tamil Nadu cites mandatory.

VERIFICATION

I, {petitioner_name}, son/daughter/wife of {petitioner_father_name}, aged about {petitioner_age} years, resident of {petitioner_address}, the Petitioner herein (filing as next friend of the detenu Shri/Smt. {detenu_name}), do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above petition are true and correct to my personal knowledge save and except such facts as are gathered from sources stated, which I believe to be true. Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Petitioner / Next Friend

promptInstructions: Draft a petition for writ of HABEAS CORPUS — the great writ of liberty. Cite Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration (1978) 4 SCC 494 — 'habeas corpus is the great writ of liberty.'
Cause-title MUST mention Article 226 (HC) and/or Article 32 (SC) read with Article 21 and Article 22.
URGENCY language must be drafted into the body — habeas listings are usually obtained within 24-48 hours.
Petitioner may be 'next friend' — relaxed locus. Cite Sheela Barse v. State of Maharashtra (1983) 2 SCC 96; any person genuinely interested can file.

Para 1: Description of parties — petitioner (next friend), detenu, State respondents. Where ordinary respondent the State, include Home Secretary, DGP, SHO of relevant PS, and if known, the detaining authority/jailer.
Para 2: Locus standi — relationship to detenu, bona fide. Petitioner not stranger; or even if stranger, public-spirited where detenu unable to approach court.
Para 3: Description of detenu — name, age, ordinary address, occupation.
Para 4-6: Factual narrative — date of last contact, circumstances of detention, search efforts, calls to PS, FIR registered or not, who confirmed detention.
Para 7: Place of detention — if known, state. If unknown, pray for direction to State to disclose. Production order can be made even without knowing exact location.
Para 8: Type of detention and illegality:
(a) Police custody beyond 24 hours without production before Magistrate — Art. 22(2) violation; S.58 BNSS [S.57 CrPC] mandate.

(b) Preventive detention — Cite Ranjit Kumar Chakraborty v. State of WB (1972) 1 SCC 1; A.K. Roy v. Union of India (1982) 1 SCC 271 (NSA constitutionality); Rekha v. State of Tamil Nadu (2011) 5 SCC 244 (preventive detention requires strict compliance). Grounds: (i) non-application of mind, (ii) delay in execution, (iii) non-communication of grounds, (iv) right to representation, (v) Advisory Board reference.
(c) Illegal private confinement — habeas lies even against private persons. Cite Mohd Ikram Hussain v. State of UP AIR 1964 SC 1625; Gohar Begum v. Suggi AIR 1960 SC 93.
(d) Illegal private confinement of adult woman — Cite Lata Singh v. State of UP (2006) 5 SCC 475 (adult woman right to choose).

(e) Child custody — habeas where retention is so unlawful that legal remedy by guardianship would be illusory; otherwise Guardians and Wards Act may be appropriate. Cite Tejaswini Gaud v. Shekhar Jagdish Prasad Tewari (2019) 7 SCC 42.
(f) Missing person with state action suspected — Cite Bhim Singh v. State of J&K (1985) 4 SCC 677 (compensation awarded for illegal detention of MLA).
Para 9: Representations made — to police (Diary No., dates), Magistrate u/S.97 BNSS [S.97 CrPC search warrant for unlawfully confined person], higher authorities. Show inadequacy / inaction.
Para 10: Article 21 (procedure not just/fair/reasonable) and Article 22 (procedural safeguards) violation.
Para 11: Urgency — every day's detention is irreparable injury to liberty. Health, communication blackout, risk to life.
Para 12: Where preventive detention — challenge specific grounds:
- Subjective satisfaction not bona fide
- Failure to communicate grounds in language detenu understands (Art. 22(5)) — Cite Hadibandhu Das v. District Magistrate (1969) 1 SCR 227.
- Delay in disposal of representation — Cite Rekha v. State of TN (2011) 5 SCC 244.
- Stale grounds / live link snapped — Cite Lakshman Khatik v. State of WB (1974) 4 SCC 1.
Prayer — production of body forthwith, declaration of illegality, liberation, compensation, disclosure.
Affidavit in support mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Life and personal liberty — substantive foundation
Protection against arrest and detention — procedural safeguards; 22(4)-(7) preventive detention
Supreme Court writ jurisdiction — fundamental right itself
Person arrested not to be detained more than 24 hours (replaces S.57 CrPC)
Search warrant for person wrongfully confined (replaces S.97 CrPC)
Arrest by police — when permissible; S.35(7) Arnesh Kumar safeguard
Grounds of order — to be communicated within 5 (extendable to 10) days; representation right

filing_checklist: Petition (original + copies per HC rules; SC: per Order XXXVIII SC Rules)
Vakalatnama / Memo of authorisation as next friend
Index, synopsis, list of dates — short for urgent listing
Photograph and identity proof of detenu
Complaints / representations to police / Magistrate with despatch proof
Where preventive detention — detention order + grounds (if served)
Affidavits of relatives confirming last contact
Mention slip for urgent listing — separately drafted
Court fee per applicable schedule (often nominal for habeas)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: petitioner_name and petitioner_relation_to_detenu must not be empty
If type_of_detention = preventive_detention_under_special_law, preventive_detention_law must not be empty
If place_of_detention_known is 'known_*', place_of_detention_address must not be empty
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
Court level limited to HC or SC
key_citations: Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration (1978) 4 SCC 494 — Great writ of liberty
Sheela Barse v. State of Maharashtra (1983) 2 SCC 96 — Locus relaxed
A.K. Roy v. Union of India (1982) 1 SCC 271 — Preventive detention constitutionality
Rekha v. State of Tamil Nadu (2011) 5 SCC 244 — Strict compliance for preventive detention
Hadibandhu Das v. District Magistrate (1969) 1 SCR 227 — Grounds in language detenu understands
Lakshman Khatik v. State of WB (1974) 4 SCC 1 — Stale grounds / live link
Bhim Singh v. State of J&K (1985) 4 SCC 677 — Compensation for illegal detention
Mohd Ikram Hussain v. State of UP AIR 1964 SC 1625 — Habeas against private persons
Gohar Begum v. Suggi AIR 1960 SC 93 — Private custody
Lata Singh v. State of UP (2006) 5 SCC 475 — Adult woman right to choose
Tejaswini Gaud v. Shekhar (2019) 7 SCC 42 — Child custody via habeas
Joginder Kumar v. State of UP (1994) 4 SCC 260 — Arrest safeguards
